It’s the only choice for fans who want full access to local, televised sports. What to know about Arizona vs. LIUArizona rolls into this matchup as one of the nation’s most complete teams. Tommy Lloyd has already set a Division I record with 141 wins in his first five seasons and delivered a Big 12 regular‑season title in Year 2 of the move. The Wildcats started 23–0, breaking their all‑time win‑streak record. They also finished 12–2 against ranked teams. They’re top‑five nationally on both sides of the ball, with elite interior scoring, rebounding, and defense.This is LIU’s first NCAA Tournament appearance since 2018, and they’re chasing the program’s first‑ever tournament win. They dominated the NEC, winning the regular‑season title by three games and then sweeping their conference tournament. Much of that success came from returning all‑conference talent (Malachi Davis, Jamal Fuller) and transfer standout Greg Gordon, the league’s Defensive Player of the Year. LIU brings real athleticism and disruptive defense, ranking 14th nationally in block percentage and 44th in steal percentage. Still, as a 16‑seed, they’re facing a mountain.This matchup is a clear clash of styles. Arizona’s frontcourt is enormous, headlined by 7‑foot‑2 Motiejus Krivas, plus versatile bigs like freshman star Koa Peat. LIU, on the other hand, leans on speed, energy, and pressure defense—despite their tallest starter being just 6′6″. Their defensive metrics show they excel at bothering teams on the perimeter and in passing lanes. But against Arizona’s interior force and elite rebounding, the question is whether LIU’s athleticism can compensate for the size deficit.Arizona scores big and often. They’ve routinely run up 90‑plus points this season and dominated non‑power opponents, winning six games by 30 or more. LIU, meanwhile, struggles from deep, averaging just six made threes per game, which makes it tough to keep pace if Arizona hits its typical rhythm. Oddsmakers aren’t shy about the gap, either. One prediction called for a 38‑point Arizona win. Can I bet on Arizona vs. LIU?Yes, Arizona is a 30.5-point favorite (-100000) over Long Island University (+8000) on FanDuel.
